A1.2 • PESSOAS PRÓXIMAS • LESSON 9 OF 11

Someone important to me

Write clearly. Ask one more question. Speak for 60-90 seconds.

Write 5-7 connected sentences.
Ask follow-up questions.
Give kind peer feedback.
Present with short notes.
1

Choose someone important

Think first. You control what you share.

4-5 min

A. Choose one option.

B. Quick notes

If yes, I will not include: Select only the type of information.

Write only the type of information, not the private detail.

Respectful language: Use kind, neutral and specific words. A fictional name or person is always OK.
2

Read the model • Lucas

Find the information and the reason.

6-7 min

1. Someone important to me is my friend, Lucas Almeida.

2. He is 24 years old, and he is from São Paulo, Brazil.

3. He is of medium height.

4. He has short wavy black hair, brown eyes, and glasses.

5. He is calm, funny, and helpful.

6. He lives in Campinas with his brother.

7. He is important to me because he always listens to me and makes me laugh.

A. Read for details.

3

Follow-up questions

Match each question to the best answer.

7-8 min

Pair practice

4

Watch and notice

British Council Speaking A1 • Talking about other people

6-7 min
First viewing: Who are the speakers talking about?
Second viewing: Listen for opinions and useful phrases.
Open video ↗
Useful phrases: Do you know…? • Yes, I do. • She's lovely. • She's very good at her job. • Good luck!

The source is British Council, but these phrases are also natural in American English.

5

Plan your paragraph

Use keywords, not complete sentences yet.

5-6 min
Reason frame: This person is important to me because…
6

Write • 5-7 sentences

Turn your notes into one clear paragraph.

8-9 min

Writer's check

7

Peer review • kind and specific

Help your partner improve one thing.

5-6 min
8

Present • 60-90 seconds

Use short notes. Look up. Pause between ideas.

7-9 min
